I need to finalize with a fine trace. Based on my investigation, the vulnerability is the undefined behavior in `get_var_int()` in `hpack-dec.c` where the shift count exceeds 32 bits, causing truncated varint values. Let me provide the trace for the PoC I tested (`/tmp/varint_test.bin`).

The PoC input is: `40 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 00` (literal header field with incremental indexing, name length varint with 10 continuation bytes triggering shift overflow, value length 0).

```json
[
  {"step": 1, "file": "fuzz_hpack_decode.c", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 55, "var": "data", "code": "memcpy(new_str, data, size); new_str[size] = '\\0';", "note": "Attacker-controlled input bytes are copied into the heap buffer new_str that is passed to hpack_decode_frame."},
  {"step": 2, "file": "fuzz_hpack_decode.c", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 66, "var": "dht", "code": "dht = hpack_dht_alloc();", "note": "A 4096-byte HPACK dynamic header table is allocated; it will receive decoded header names/values."},
  {"step": 3, "file": "fuzz_hpack_decode.c", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 70, "var": "new_str", "code": "hpack_decode_frame(dht, new_str, size, list, sizeof(list)/sizeof(list[0]), &tmp);", "note": "The raw input is handed to the HPACK decoder; the first byte 0x40 selects a literal header field with incremental indexing."},
  {"step": 4, "file": "src/hpack-dec.c", "function": "hpack_decode_frame", "line": 260, "var": "raw", "code": "huff = *raw & 0x80; nlen = get_var_int(&raw, &len, 7);", "note": "The decoder reads the name-length varint; the first byte 0xff has the huffman bit set and all 7 low bits set, so the loop will consume continuation bytes."},
  {"step": 5, "file": "src/hpack-dec.c", "function": "get_var_int", "line": 67, "var": "shift", "code": "ret += ((uint32_t)(*raw++) & 127) << shift;", "note": "Each 0xff continuation byte contributes 127 << shift; after 5 continuation bytes shift reaches 35, exceeding the 32-bit width of the shift operand."},
  {"step": 6, "file": "src/hpack-dec.c", "function": "get_var_int", "line": 67, "var": "ret", "code": "ret += ((uint32_t)(*raw++) & 127) << shift;", "note": "shift exponent 35 (and later 63) is undefined behavior for a 32-bit unsigned int; on x86 the shift is taken modulo 32, producing a truncated/wrong nlen value."},
  {"step": 7, "file": "src/hpack-dec.c", "function": "get_var_int", "line": 76, "var": "shift", "code": "shift += 7;", "note": "shift keeps increasing by 7 per continuation byte, so the undefined shift count grows (35, 42, 49, 56, 63) as long as the high bit of each byte is set."},

  {"step": 9, "file": "src/hpack-dec.c", "function": "hpack_decode_frame", "line": 264, "var": "name", "code": "name = ist2(raw, nlen); raw += nlen; len -= nlen;", "note": "The decoder treats nlen bytes starting after the continuation bytes as the header name, desynchronizing the stream position from the actual encoded data."},
  {"step": 10, "file": "src/hpack-dec.c", "function": "hpack_decode_frame", "line": 275, "var": "ntrash", "code": "nlen = huff_dec((const uint8_t *)name.ptr, name.len, ntrash, tmp->size - tmp->data);", "note": "The mis-sized name is huffman-decoded into the tmp buffer; the wrong length and stream position feed inconsistent data into the decoder."},
```
